name: GitHub
steps: Click your profile picture, then Settings
Open Password and authentication
In the Two-factor authentication section, start the setup and choose the authenticator app option
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes

name: GitLab
steps: Click your avatar, then Edit profile, then Access > Password and authentication
In One-time password authenticator, click Register authenticator
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Enter your current password
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Your email must be verified first. GitLab also asks for your current password with the code.

name: Facebook
steps: Click your profile picture, then Settings and privacy, then Settings
In Accounts Center, open Password and security, then Two-factor authentication
Pick the account, then choose the authentication app option
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Facebook can also give you 10 recovery login codes.

name: Instagram
steps: Open Settings, then Accounts Center
Tap Password and security, then Two-factor authentication
Pick your account and choose the authentication app option
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Shares settings with your Meta Account in Accounts Center.

name: Google
steps: Open your Google Account and go to Security
Turn on 2-Step Verification and finish the prompts
Back on the 2-Step Verification page, choose Authenticator app and tap Set up authenticator
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
notes: Google's own page for adding an authenticator app is the same page that turns on 2-Step Verification.

name: Slack
steps: Sign in to your workspace and open your Account settings page
Next to Two-factor Authentication, click Expand, then Set Up Two-Factor Authentication
Enter your password and click Use an app
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
notes: Each workspace needs its own 2FA setup.

name: DigitalOcean
steps: Sign in to the control panel and open your account security settings
Turn on two-factor authentication and choose Authenticator app
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: DigitalOcean also asks you to add a backup method after you set the first one.

name: Cloudflare
steps: Go to Profile, then Authentication
Under Two-Factor Authentication, click Set up
Under Mobile App Authentication, click Add and enter your Cloudflare password
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Cloudflare calls the recovery codes backup codes.

name: Amazon Web Services
steps: Sign in to the AWS console and open Security credentials
Choose to assign an MFA device and pick Authenticator app
Click Show QR code in the setup wizard
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
notes: Shown for the account owner (root) sign-in. AWS asks for two codes in a row; wait for the next code before typing the second.

name: Bitwarden
steps: Log in to the Bitwarden web app
Go to Settings, then Security, then Two-step login
Find Authenticator App and click Manage, then enter your master password
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Bitwarden also shows a recovery code on the Two-step login screen; save it right away. Don't store this code in Bitwarden itself.

name: 1Password
steps: Sign in at 1Password.com and click your name, then Manage Account
Choose More Actions, then Manage Two-Factor Authentication
Click Set Up App
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
notes: Write down the 16-character secret shown next to the QR code and keep it somewhere safe. Use a different app than 1Password to hold this code.

name: Notion
steps: In Notion, open Settings and click your name
Under Account security, turn on 2-step verification
Choose Authenticator
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Notion asks you to name the method, and shows backup codes with your first method.

name: Heroku
steps: Open Account Settings
Click Setup Multi-Factor Authentication
Next to the authenticator app method, click Add and follow the prompts
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Heroku recommends adding a second verification method as a backup.

name: Vercel
steps: Open your Vercel account settings
Turn on the two-factor authentication switch and choose Authenticator App
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes

name: Atlassian
steps: Open your Atlassian account security page and click Manage two-step verification
Enter your password and click Set up
Choose the authenticator app method
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
notes: Atlassian gives you an emergency recovery key. Save it somewhere safe.

name: Yahoo
steps: Open your Yahoo Account Security page
Under Ways of signing in, click 2-step verification
Choose Authenticator app and click Continue
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
notes: Yahoo needs at least two recovery methods on the account before this option shows up.

name: WordPress.com
steps: Open Security, then Two-Step Authentication in your WordPress.com account
Click Set up using an app
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: WordPress.com makes you confirm one backup code to finish.

name: Docker Hub
steps: Sign in to your Docker account and open your account security settings
Turn on two-factor authentication
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Docker gives you one recovery code. After 2FA is on, command-line logins need a personal access token.

name: Dropbox
steps: Log in at dropbox.com (this can't be done in the app)
Click your avatar, then Settings, then the Security tab
Switch on 2-factor authentication and re-enter your password
Choose Use an authenticator app
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes

name: Tumblr
steps: Open Settings and find the Security section
Turn on Two-factor authentication and enter your password
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
notes: Tumblr backup codes come from the Generate backup codes button in Security.

name: Proton
steps: Sign in at account.proton.me and open Settings
Choose Account and password, then find Two-factor authentication
Turn on the Authenticator app option and enter your password
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Proton asks for your password again along with the code.

name: Namecheap
steps: Sign in to Namecheap and go to Profile, then Security
In the Access section, find Two-Factor Authentication and click Manage
Choose the Authentication app (TOTP) option and enter your password
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Namecheap also offers backup codes after setup.

name: Kraken
steps: Sign in to Kraken and open Security
Under Sign-in Two-Factor Authentication, click Enable next to Authenticator app
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
notes: Kraken says the setup key is your backup for the app; treat it like a password.

name: Stripe
steps: Sign in to the Stripe Dashboard and open Personal details
In Two-step authentication, add a method and choose Authenticator app
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Stripe gives you a backup code during setup.

name: Figma
steps: Click your name at the top left of the file browser and choose Settings
Open the Security tab and click Enable two-factor authentication
Choose the authenticator app option and enter your password
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Not available if you sign in with Google or SAML single sign-on.

name: LinkedIn
steps: Click your profile icon, then Settings & Privacy
Under Sign-in & security, choose Two-step verification
Turn it on, choose Authenticator App, and enter your password
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
notes: LinkedIn may show a secret key instead of a QR code on some screens; Tanooki Auth can also add accounts by typing the key.

name: PayPal
steps: Log in to PayPal on the web
Click the Settings icon, then Security
Next to 2-step verification, click Set Up, then choose Use an authenticator app
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish

name: Snapchat
steps: Open Snapchat, go to your profile, then Settings
Tap My Account, then Two-Factor Authentication, then Continue
Choose Authentication App
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
notes: You need a phone number and email on the account first. Snapchat uses a separate Recovery Code that you create under the same setting; using it turns 2FA off.

name: Twitch
steps: Open Settings, then Security and Privacy
Turn on Two-Factor Authentication and finish the text-message check first
Then choose the authenticator app option
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Twitch requires a phone number first, and landline numbers don't work.

name: Zoom
steps: Sign in to the Zoom web portal and open your Profile
Under Sign In, turn on Two-Step Verification
Click Set Up next to Authentication App and enter your password
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Needs a paid plan, and the account admin may need to turn it on first.

name: Mailchimp
steps: Open your Mailchimp Account security page
Choose Authenticator app under 2-factor authentication and click Next
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Once on, Mailchimp 2FA can't be turned off, only changed.

name: Squarespace
steps: Open your Squarespace account settings and find Two-factor authentication
Click Set Up next to Authentication App
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes

name: Etsy
steps: Open Account settings, then Security
Under 2 factor authentication, choose Turn on 2FA
Pick Authenticator App
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Etsy asks you to press Confirm and then Complete.

name: Netlify
steps: Open User settings, then Security
Under Two-factor authentication, turn it on
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Netlify shows recovery codes only once.

name: Twilio
steps: Open User Settings in the Twilio Console
In Two-factor authentication, click Edit and choose to add an authenticator app (listed as Another authenticator app)
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Twilio gives a recovery code when you first turn it on.

name: Wix
steps: Open Account Settings and find 2-step verification
Turn on the authenticator app option and enter your Wix password
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
notes: If you remove the Wix account from the app, you can't use this method to sign in until you use Reset App.

name: PlayStation
steps: Sign in to Account Management and open Security
Edit your 2-step verification status and choose the authenticator app method
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: PlayStation gives 10 single-use backup codes.

name: Nintendo
steps: Sign in to your Nintendo Account on the web and open Sign-in and security settings
Open 2-Step Verification and start the setup
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Nintendo only tests Google Authenticator, but its codes follow the standard, so Tanooki Auth should also work. Child accounts can't use it.

name: Binance
steps: Sign in to Binance and open Security
Next to Google Authenticator, click Enable
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: Binance calls it Google Authenticator but any standard app works. It shows a backup key; write it down.

name: Akamai Cloud (Linode)
steps: Click your username in Cloud Manager and choose Login & Authentication
Set the login method to Cloud Manager and turn on two-factor authentication
Scan the QR code with Tanooki Auth (tap +, then Scan QR)
Type the 6-digit code from Tanooki Auth to finish
Save the recovery codes. In Tanooki Auth you can store them in the account's Recovery codes
notes: You must set up security questions first. Akamai shows a scratch code to keep as your backup.
